Entry 5: Place Index Part 2: Venus
Venus. For so long, it was a wasteland, uninhabitable by man. With almost contant volcanic activity and extreme heat...
No wonder we wanted to colonize it.
We humans managed to turn it into a second Earth, which some theorize to be the orignal state of Venus.
However, with the war of them demons and aliens, Venus went back to being a wasteland.
You can still live on Venus if you wanted to, but do you really want to? There is barely any vegitation because it was all burnt up.
There is barely anyone living on the planet, and there are barely any resources or water anymore on the planet.
However, Venus is still very important for one reason: Vorp Slime
Vorp slime, the dead baby single-celled offspring of the 1 foot long multicellar offspring of the "Geleizoogdierspinen". 
They are like spiders, but look like jelly and give off massive amounts of radiation and heat.
Even their offspring do, which start out as single cells.
Mother geleizoogdierspinen give birth to massive clumps and colonies of baby geleizoogdierspinen. 
Which can be found on the walls of caves or volcanos. 
Mother geleizoogdierspinen make so much babies at once that the colonies look like massive amounts of slime.
Baby geleizoogdierspinen (aka vorp slime) can be used as infinite, clean, and resourceful sources of nuclear energy. 
The energy made from vorp slime can be converted with anthro, chaos, or isorropian energy to make more anthro energy. 
This makes Venus the second most important planet apart from Earth right now.
Some theorize that the geleizoogdierspinen are heavily evolved and mutated decendants of the bacteria clinging to sputnik.
(The first artifical satellite, which was made in the USSR)
A missing chunk of sputnik was found on Venus, so it could check out.
Fun fact: the term "vorp slime", originates from the Dutch word, "worp" (pronounced "vorp"), 
which means, "the act of a mammal giving birth."
All in all, Venus is a very interesting planet with a facisnating history and it's importance will never be taken for granted.
